text: Understood what we are saying, we repeat, right? Once, two, three times, whatever, but we repeat, and that is sadly the simplest form of coding that you can apply. So in wireless transmissions, they do that, even in the in the more sophisticated generations of wireless technologies, they do that. There is the technique of repeating. So this is the string of useful bits, the ones that you really want to transfer. They are user bits, they are the valuable bits, and if you repeat them twice more, these are redundant bits, right? So the one with the green background are redundant bits. And then what the receiver does in this case is try to modulate these useful bits, right? Once, and then it modulates this row, and then it modulates this row, and then depending on what it has modulated, on what it has understood. For each bit, it applies a majority rule. So for example, if the receiver has modulated the first bit of these rows twice as zero and once as one, it will say, well, the result is zero because twice I modulated the bit as zero and once I modulated as one. So likely I made a mistake.
